zh.title: 空中巴士A330neo比波音787-9便宜多少 真實成本不在牌價上
zh.summary: 波音787-9訂單量（1,493架）遠勝空中巴士A330-900（511架），全新機市場價值也高出約3,200萬至4,100萬美元；但牌價並不可靠，真正的成本取決於市場價、租賃費率與航空公司的機隊結構——以每飛行小時約1.3萬美元估算，兩者營運成本其實相去不遠。
body: 兩款廣體客機是直接競爭對手。波音787-9訂單達1,493架，遠多於A330-900的511架，市場價值也較高，且787-9是全新設計的複合材料飛機；A330neo則是1980年代設計的A330大幅改良版，換上新發動機、新機翼與新航電系統，但機身仍以鋁合金為主。從牌價看，A330-900為2.964億美元（2018年），787-9為2.925億美元（2019年），幾乎相同；但牌價只是談判起點，製造商實際上從不以牌價出售，航空公司與租賃商也不會按牌價付款，真正該看的是市場價與租賃費率。

以IBA的估值，新交付的A330-900市場價值約1.185億美元，787-9則在1.51億至1.6億美元之間；最老的A330-900（2018年出廠）約7,310萬美元，最老的787-9（2014年出廠）約7,060萬美元，二手價反而相近。月租費率方面，全新787-9約105萬至116萬美元，A330neo約90萬至99萬美元；中齡機787-9約69.5萬至79.2萬美元，A330neo約60萬至75.6萬美元。2026年市場價值普遍上漲：787-9年增7%、A350-900增5%、777-300ER增24%、A330-300增20%，A330neo的月租費率漲幅更達13%，主因是空中巴士與波音生產瓶頸導致交付期延至2030年初。

不過，誰的營運成本較低並沒有標準答案。兩款飛機的三艙等典型座位數相近（A330-900為260至300席，787-9為250至290席），最大起飛重量幾乎相同（251噸對254噸），787-9航程略勝一籌，但多數任務都在A330neo航程之內。機隊共通性往往才是關鍵：若航空公司同時營運舊款A330與A350，空中巴士宣稱A330ceo與A330neo備件共通率高達95%、飛行員型別檢定相同，A321neo與A330neo搭配營運更可降低最多30%營運成本；反觀波音777與787之間沒有共通型別檢定，787也須專用工具。粗略估算，兩款飛機每飛行小時營運成本都在1.3萬美元上下、誤差數千美元，勝負完全取決於航空公司的個別條件。

en.title: The true cost of an Airbus A330neo compared with a Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner
en.summary: The Boeing 787-9 has a much larger order book than the Airbus A330-900 — 1,493 aircraft against 511 — and a new 787-9 is worth roughly $32–41 million more. But list prices are meaningless; the real comparison runs through market values, lease rates and each airline's fleet structure, and on a rough per-flight-hour basis the two are surprisingly close.
body: The Airbus A330-900 and the Boeing 787-9 are close competitors, yet on the face of it the Dreamliner looks well ahead: 1,493 orders against 511 for the A330-900, a higher market value, and a cleansheet composite design, while the A330neo is a comprehensive update of the 1980s-designed A330, with new engines, new wings and new avionics but a mostly aluminium fuselage. Their list prices are almost identical — $296.4 million for the A330-900 in 2018 and $292.5 million for the 787-9 in 2019 — but list prices are inflated sticker prices that manufacturers never actually sell at and airlines and lessors never pay, so they are a poor guide to what an aircraft really costs.

Market values tell a different story. In the first quarter of 2026, IBA put a newly delivered A330-900 at $118.5 million, against $151–160 million for a new 787-9; the oldest A330-900s, built in 2018, are worth about $73.1 million, while the oldest 787-9s, built in 2014, are worth about $70.6 million — the used values are close. Monthly lease rates for a new 787-9 run around $1.05–1.16 million against $900,000–$990,000 for the A330neo, and at mid-age about $695,000–$792,000 against $600,000–$756,000. Widebody values have risen sharply as production bottlenecks at Airbus and Boeing push delivery dates for many recent orders as far back as early 2030: IBA reported 2026 market values up 7% for the 787-9, 5% for the A350-900, 24% for the 777-300ER and 20% for the A330-300, with A330neo lease rates up by as much as 13%.

Even so, there is no single answer to which aircraft costs less to operate. Typical three-class seating is close — 260–300 for the A330-900 and 250–290 for the 787-9 — and maximum takeoff weights are almost identical at 251 and 254 tonnes, with the 787-9 holding only a modest range advantage that matters in edge cases. Fleet commonality often decides it: an airline that also flies older A330s and new A350s benefits from Airbus's claim of up to 95% commonality in A330ceo/A330neo spare parts and the same pilot type rating across the generations, and Airbus says that "Today, the A321neo and the A330neo have proven to deliver up to 30% lower operating costs when operated together." Boeing's 777 and 787, by contrast, share no common type rating, and the 787 needs dedicated tooling. On back-of-the-envelope maths, both airliners likely cost around $13,000 per flight hour to operate, plus or minus a few thousand dollars — the winner is highly contingent.
